translations.idiomatic: Biography 61 — Loyalty and Righteousness, Part 3: Tu Danhang; Wanyan Chenheshang; Yang Woyan; Wugulun Heihan; Tuoman Hutumen; Ji Ruzuo; Ai Shen; Ma Jianlong

translations.idiomatic: (Supplementary biographies)

sentences.zh: 禹顯 張邦憲 劉全

translations.literal: Yu Xian, Zhang Bangxian, Liu Quan
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xian; Zhang Bangxian; Liu Quan

sentences.zh: 徒單航

translations.literal: Tu Danhang
translations.idiomatic: Tu Danhang

sentences.zh: 完顏陳和尚

translations.literal: Wanyan Chenheshang
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Chenheshang

sentences.zh: 完顏陳和尚，名彝，字良佐，亦以小字行，豐州人。

translations.literal: Wanyan Chenheshang, given name Yi, courtesy name Liangzuo, also known by his childhood name, was a native of Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Chenheshang, whose given name was Yi and courtesy name Liangzuo, was commonly known by his childhood name. He came from Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 系出蕭王諸孫。

translations.literal: He was descended from the various grandsons of Prince Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: His lineage traced to the grandsons of Prince Xiao.

sentences.zh: 父乞哥，泰和南征，以功授同知階州軍事，及宋複階州，乞哥戰歿于嘉陵江。

translations.literal: His father Qige, on the southern campaign in the Taihe era, was appointed by merit as Vice Commissioner of Jiezhou Military Affairs; when Song recovered Jiezhou, Qige died in battle on the Jialing River.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qige served on the southern campaigns of the Taihe reign and, for his achievements, was made vice commissioner of military affairs at Jiezhou. When the Song retook Jiezhou, Qige was killed in action on the Jialing River.

sentences.zh: 貞祐中，陳和尚年二十余，為北兵所掠，大帥甚愛之，置帳下。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyou era, Chenheshang was a little over twenty and was captured by the northern troops; the supreme commander took a great liking to him and kept him in his personal retinue.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenyou period, when Chenheshang was in his early twenties, northern forces captured him. Their supreme commander grew very fond of him and kept him in his own camp.

sentences.zh: 時陳和尚母留豐州，從兄安平都尉斜烈事之甚謹。

translations.literal: At that time Chenheshang's mother remained in Fengzhou, and his cousin Xielie, Anping Commandant, attended her with great care.
translations.idiomatic: His mother stayed behind in Fengzhou, where his cousin Xielie, commandant of Anping, looked after her with scrupulous devotion.

sentences.zh: 陳和尚在北歲餘，托以省母，乞還。

translations.literal: After more than a year in the north, Chenheshang pleaded to return on the pretext of visiting his mother.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year with the northern army, Chenheshang asked leave to go home, saying he wished to visit his mother.

sentences.zh: 大帥以卒監之至豐，乃與斜烈劫殺監卒。

translations.literal: The supreme commander sent soldiers to escort him as far as Feng; there he and Xielie ambushed and killed the escorts.
translations.idiomatic: The commander sent troops to escort him to Fengzhou. There Chenheshang and Xielie fell upon the escort and killed them.

sentences.zh: 奪馬奉其母南奔，大兵覺，合騎追之，由他路得免。

translations.literal: They seized horses, took his mother, and fled south; when the great army realized it, they joined cavalry in pursuit, but by another route he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: They seized horses, placed his mother upon one, and fled south. The enemy soon gave chase with combined cavalry, but they slipped away by another route.

sentences.zh: 既而失馬，母老不能行，載以鹿角車，兄弟共挽，南渡河。

translations.literal: Soon afterward they lost their horses; his mother was old and could not walk, so they loaded her on a deer-antler cart and the brothers hauled it together, crossing the river southward.
translations.idiomatic: They soon lost their horses. His mother was too old to walk, so they put her in a deer-antler sled and the brothers hauled it together across the river to the south.

sentences.zh: 宣宗奇之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong marveled at this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong was astonished by the feat.

sentences.zh: 斜烈以世官授都統，陳和尚試補護衛，未幾轉奉禦。

translations.literal: Xielie received the post of commander-in-chief through hereditary office; Chenheshang entered service on probation as a guardsman and before long was transferred to palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Xielie inherited the post of commander-in-chief, while Chenheshang entered service as a probationary guardsman and soon became a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 及斜烈行壽、泗元帥府事，奏陳和尚自隨，詔以充宣差提控，佩金符。

translations.literal: When Xielie took charge of the Shou-Si Marshal's headquarters, he memorialized that Chenheshang should accompany him; an edict appointed him as an imperial commissioner and military controller, with a gold tally.
translations.idiomatic: When Xielie took charge of the Shou-Si marshal's headquarters, he asked that Chenheshang accompany him. The court appointed Chenheshang an imperial commissioner and military controller and granted him a gold tally.

sentences.zh: 斜烈辟太原王渥為經歷。

translations.literal: Xielie recruited Wang Wo of Taiyuan as his administrative officer.
translations.idiomatic: Xielie engaged Wang Wo of Taiyuan as his administrative officer.

sentences.zh: 渥字仲澤，文章論議與雷淵、李獻能相上下，故得師友之。

translations.literal: Wo, courtesy name Zhongze, in literary composition and discourse was the equal of Lei Yuan and Li Xianneng, and therefore Chenheshang treated him as teacher and friend.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wo, courtesy name Zhongze, ranked with Lei Yuan and Li Xianneng in literary skill and debate, and Chenheshang treated him as both teacher and friend.

sentences.zh: 陳和尚天資高明，雅好文史，自居禁衛日，人以秀才目之。

translations.literal: Chenheshang was gifted by nature and fond of literature and history; from the days he served in the inner guard, people regarded him as a scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Naturally gifted and devoted to literature and history, Chenheshang had been regarded as a scholar ever since his days in the inner guard.

sentences.zh: 至是，渥授以《孝經》、《小學》、《論語》、《春秋左氏傳》，略通其義。

translations.literal: At this time Wo instructed him in the Classic of Filial Piety, the Elementary Learning, the Analects, and Zuo's Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals, and he came to grasp their meaning in outline.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wo now taught him the Classic of Filial Piety, the Elementary Learning, the Analects, and Zuo's Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals, and Chenheshang gained a working understanding of them.

sentences.zh: 軍中無事，則窗下作牛毛細字，如寒苦之士，其視世味漠然。

translations.literal: When the army had no duties, he would write tiny characters like ox hair by the window, like a poor scholar in hardship, and he looked on worldly pleasures with indifference.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the camp was idle, he would sit at the window writing characters fine as ox hair, like a scholar in poverty, and worldly pleasures left him unmoved.

sentences.zh: 正大二年，斜烈落帥職，例為總領，屯方城。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengda, Xielie was removed from command and, by precedent, became a chief administrator, stationed at Fangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Zhengda reign, Xielie was relieved of command and, by precedent, became chief administrator, with his forces encamped at Fangcheng.

sentences.zh: 陳和尚隨以往，凡兄軍中事皆預知之。

translations.literal: Chenheshang accompanied him; he was privy beforehand to all his elder brother's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chenheshang went with him and was kept informed of every matter in his cousin's command.

sentences.zh: 斜烈時在病，軍中李太和者，與方城鎮防軍葛宜翁相毆，訴于陳和尚，宜翁事不直，即量笞之。

translations.literal: Xielie was then ill; in the army one Li Taihe had come to blows with Ge Yiweng of the Fangcheng garrison defense force and appealed to Chenheshang; Yiweng was in the wrong, and Chenheshang at once had him beaten in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: Xielie was ill at the time. A soldier named Li Taihe had fought with Ge Yiweng of the Fangcheng garrison and brought the case to Chenheshang. Finding Yiweng in the wrong, Chenheshang had him beaten on the spot.

sentences.zh: 宜翁素兇悍，恥以理屈受杖，竟鬱鬱以死，留語其妻，必報陳和尚。

translations.literal: Yiweng had always been fierce and overbearing; he was ashamed to take a beating when he was in the wrong and in the end died of brooding, leaving word to his wife that she must avenge him on Chenheshang.
translations.idiomatic: Yiweng had always been brutal and overbearing. Ashamed to be beaten when he was clearly in the wrong, he brooded himself to death, telling his wife she must have revenge on Chenheshang.

sentences.zh: 妻訟陳和尚以私忿侵官，故殺其夫，訴於台省，於近侍，積薪龍津橋南，約不得報，則自焚以謝其夫。

translations.literal: His wife accused Chenheshang of using private resentment to overstep his office and deliberately killing her husband; she appealed to the Censorate and to the inner attendants, piled firewood south of Longjin Bridge, and pledged that if she received no redress she would burn herself to answer to her husband.
translations.idiomatic: His wife accused Chenheshang of abusing his authority out of private spite and deliberately causing her husband's death. She appealed to the Censorate and to the palace attendants, piled firewood south of Longjin Bridge, and vowed to burn herself if she received no justice for her husband.

sentences.zh: 以故陳和尚系獄。

translations.literal: For this reason Chenheshang was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: For this Chenheshang was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 議者疑陳和尚，狃于禁近，倚兵閫之重，必橫恣違法，當以大辟。

translations.literal: Those who deliberated suspected Chenheshang, accustomed to proximity to the throne and relying on the weight of military command, would certainly act lawlessly and should receive the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Counselors suspected that Chenheshang, accustomed to palace proximity and backed by a powerful command, must have acted with arrogant lawlessness and deserved execution.

sentences.zh: 奏上，久不能決。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted, but for a long time no decision could be reached.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went up, yet for a long time the court could reach no decision.

sentences.zh: 陳和尚聚書獄中讀之，凡十有八月。

translations.literal: Chenheshang gathered books in prison and read them, altogether eighteen months.
translations.idiomatic: Chenheshang gathered books in his cell and read for eighteen months.

sentences.zh: 明年，斜烈病癒，詔提兵而西，入朝，哀宗怪其瘦甚，問：「卿甯以方城獄未決故耶？

translations.literal: The next year Xielie recovered from illness; an edict ordered him to lead troops westward, and on entering court Emperor Aizong was struck by how thin he had become and asked, "Are you perhaps still troubled because the Fangcheng case has not been decided?
translations.idiomatic: The following year Xielie recovered and was ordered west with the army. When he came to court, Emperor Aizong was shocked at how thin he had grown and asked, "Is it because the Fangcheng case still hangs unresolved?

sentences.zh: 卿但行，吾今赦之矣。

translations.literal: You need only go; I shall pardon him now.
translations.idiomatic: Go on your way — I shall pardon him now.

sentences.zh: 」以台諫複有言，不敢赦。

translations.literal: " Because the censorate and remonstrance officials spoke again, he did not dare to pardon him.
translations.idiomatic: " But the censorate and remonstrance officials spoke up again, and the emperor did not dare to grant the pardon.

sentences.zh: 未幾，斜烈卒。

translations.literal: Before long Xielie died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xielie died.

sentences.zh: 上聞，始馳赦陳和尚，曰：「有司奏汝以私忿殺人。

translations.literal: On hearing this, the emperor at last hastened to pardon Chenheshang, saying, "The authorities reported that you killed a man out of private resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard the news, the emperor at last sent a hurried pardon to Chenheshang, saying, "The authorities reported that you killed a man out of private spite.

sentences.zh: 汝兄死，失吾一名將。

translations.literal: Your elder brother has died, and I have lost a great general.
translations.idiomatic: Your cousin is dead, and I have lost a great general.

sentences.zh: 今以汝兄故，曲法赦汝，天下必有議我者。

translations.literal: Now for your elder brother's sake I bend the law to pardon you; there will surely be those in the realm who criticize me.
translations.idiomatic: For your cousin's sake I now bend the law to pardon you. There will surely be those in the realm who criticize me for it.

sentences.zh: 他日，汝奮發立功名，國家得汝力，始以我為不妄赦矣。

translations.literal: Another day, if you exert yourself and establish merit and fame, and the state gains your strength, then they will know I did not pardon you rashly.
translations.idiomatic: If one day you throw yourself into service and win merit and fame, and the state gains your strength, then they will know I did not pardon you in vain.

sentences.zh: 」陳和尚且泣且拜，悲動左右，不能出一言為謝。

translations.literal: " Chenheshang wept as he bowed, moving those around him to grief, and could not utter a word of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: " Chenheshang wept as he bowed, moving all who stood by to tears, and could not find a word of thanks.

sentences.zh: 乃以白衣領紫微軍都統，逾年轉忠孝軍提控。

translations.literal: He was then made commander of the Ziwei Army in plain dress, and after a year was transferred to military controller of the Zhongxiao Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was then placed in command of the Ziwei Army while still in plain dress, and a year later was made military controller of the Zhongxiao Army.

sentences.zh: 五年，北兵入大昌原，平章合達問誰可為前鋒者，陳和尚出應命。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, northern troops entered Dachangyuan; the Grand Councilor Heda asked who could serve as vanguard, and Chenheshang stepped forward to answer the call.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, northern forces entered Dachangyuan. Grand Councilor Heda asked who could lead the vanguard, and Chenheshang stepped forward.

sentences.zh: 先已沐浴易衣，若將就木然者，擐甲上馬不反顧。

translations.literal: He had already bathed and changed his clothes as if about to enter his coffin; he donned armor, mounted his horse, and did not look back.
translations.idiomatic: He had already bathed and changed his clothes as though preparing for his coffin. He buckled on his armor, mounted, and rode off without a backward glance.

sentences.zh: 是日，以四百騎破八千眾，三軍之士踴躍思戰，蓋自軍興二十年始有此捷。

translations.literal: That day with four hundred horsemen he defeated eight thousand; the troops of the three armies leaped with eagerness to fight — for twenty years since the armies were raised there had been no victory like this.
translations.idiomatic: That day four hundred horsemen under his command routed eight thousand. The whole army brimmed with eagerness to fight — the first such victory in twenty years of war.

sentences.zh: 奏功第一，手詔褒諭，授定遠大將軍、平涼府判官，世襲謀克。

translations.literal: His merit was reported first; an imperial autograph commended him; he was appointed General Who Stabilizes the Distance and judge of Pingliang Prefecture, with hereditary mouke status.
translations.idiomatic: His merit was reported first in the dispatch. The emperor wrote him a personal commendation and appointed him General Who Stabilizes the Distance and judge of Pingliang Prefecture, with hereditary mouke status.

sentences.zh: 一日名動天下。

translations.literal: In a single day his name shook the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In a single day his name resounded throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 忠孝一軍，皆回紇、乃滿、羌、渾及中原被俘避罪來歸者，鷙狠淩突，號難制。

translations.literal: The entire Zhongxiao Army consisted of Uyghurs, Naimans, Qiang, Hun, and men from the Central Plains who had been captured, fled punishment, and come over — fierce, brutal, and overbearing, known as hard to control.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhongxiao Army was made up of Uyghurs, Naimans, Qiang, Hun, and men from the Central Plains who had been captured or fled punishment to join the Jin — fierce, brutal, and overbearing, and notoriously hard to control.

sentences.zh: 陳和尚禦之有方，坐作進退皆中程式，所過州邑常料所給外秋毫無犯，街曲間不復喧雜，每戰則先登陷陣，疾若風雨，諸軍倚以為重。

translations.literal: Chenheshang had effective methods for controlling them; in sitting, rising, advancing, and retreating all conformed to regulations; in the prefectures and districts he passed, beyond the regular rations supplied he did not violate the slightest thing, and the lanes were no longer noisy; in every battle he was first to charge and break the enemy line, swift as wind and rain, and the armies relied on him as their mainstay.
translations.idiomatic: Chenheshang governed them with skill. In camp and on the march they followed regulations to the letter. Wherever he passed, his men took nothing beyond the regular rations, and the streets fell quiet. In every battle he was first into the breach, swift as wind and rain, and the armies looked to him as their pillar.

sentences.zh: 六年，有衛州之勝。

translations.literal: In the sixth year there was the victory at Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year came the victory at Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 八年，有倒回穀之勝。

translations.literal: In the eighth year there was the victory at Daohuigu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year came the victory at Daohuigu.

sentences.zh: 自刑徒不四五遷為禦侮中郎將。

translations.literal: From a convicted criminal, in no more than four or five promotions he became General of the Guard against Insult.
translations.idiomatic: From convicted criminal to General of the Guard against Insult he rose in scarcely four or five steps.

sentences.zh: 副樞移剌蒲阿無持重之略，嘗一日夜馳二百里趨小利，軍中莫敢諫止。

translations.literal: Vice Marshal Yila Pu'a lacked a strategy of steady weight; he once rode two hundred li in a day and night to pursue small gains, and in the army none dared remonstrate and stop him.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Marshal Yila Pu'a lacked a steady strategic mind. Once he rode two hundred li in a day and a night chasing petty gains, and no one in the army dared to stop him.

sentences.zh: 陳和尚私謂同列曰：「副樞以大將軍為剽略之事，今日得生口三百，明日得牛羊一二千，士卒喘死者則不復計。

translations.literal: Chenheshang said privately to his peers, "The vice marshal uses a great general for marauding raids; today he takes three hundred captives, tomorrow one or two thousand cattle and sheep, while soldiers who die gasping for breath are no longer counted.
translations.idiomatic: Chenheshang said privately to his peers, "The vice marshal uses a great general for raiding. Today three hundred captives, tomorrow a thousand or two head of cattle and sheep — and the men who drop dead from exhaustion are not counted at all.

sentences.zh: 國家數年所積，一旦必為是人破除盡矣。

translations.literal: What the state has accumulated over several years will in one stroke surely be squandered to the last by such a man.
translations.idiomatic: What the state has built up over years will be squandered to nothing by such a man in a single stroke.

sentences.zh: 」或以告蒲阿，一日，置酒會諸將飲，酒行至陳和尚，蒲阿曰：「汝曾短長我，又謂國家兵力當由我盡壞，誠有否？

translations.literal: " Someone reported this to Pu'a; one day he set out wine and gathered the generals to drink; when the cup reached Chenheshang, Pu'a said, "You once spoke ill of me and also said the state's military strength would be ruined entirely by me — is that truly so?
translations.idiomatic: " Someone reported this to Pu'a. One day he set out wine for the generals, and when the cup reached Chenheshang, Pu'a said, "You once spoke ill of me and said the state's military strength would be ruined entirely by me — is that true?

sentences.zh: 」陳和尚飲畢，徐曰「有。

translations.literal: " Chenheshang finished his drink and said slowly, "It is so.
translations.idiomatic: " Chenheshang drained his cup and said calmly, "It is so.

sentences.zh: 」蒲阿見其無懼容，漫為好語雲：「有過當面論，無後言也。」

translations.literal: " Pu'a saw that he showed no fear and casually spoke friendly words: "If there is fault, discuss it to my face; do not speak behind my back."
translations.idiomatic: " Pu'a saw he showed no fear and made light friendly talk: "If you find fault, say it to my face — none of this talk behind my back."

sentences.zh: 九年正月，三峰山之敗，走鈞州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year, after the defeat at Sanfeng Mountain, he fled to Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year, after the defeat at Sanfeng Mountain, he fled to Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 城破，大兵入，即縱軍巷戰。

translations.literal: When the city fell and the great army entered, he at once let his troops fight in the lanes.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell and the enemy entered, he at once ordered street fighting.

sentences.zh: 陳和尚趨避隱處，殺掠稍定乃出，自言曰：「我金國大將，欲見白事。

translations.literal: Chenheshang hurried to a hidden place; when the killing and plundering had subsided somewhat he came out and said of himself, "I am a great general of the Jin state and wish to report business.
translations.idiomatic: Chenheshang hid until the slaughter had subsided, then came out and declared, "I am a great general of the Jin and wish to make a report.

sentences.zh: 」兵士以數騎夾之，詣行帳前。

translations.literal: " Soldiers flanked him with several horsemen and brought him before the field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: " Soldiers took him under escort of several horsemen to the field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 問其姓名，曰：「我忠孝軍總領陳和尚也。

translations.literal: Asked his name, he said, "I am Chenheshang, commander of the Zhongxiao Army.
translations.idiomatic: Asked his name, he said, "I am Chenheshang, commander of the Zhongxiao Army.

sentences.zh: 大昌原之勝者我也，衛州之勝亦我也，倒回穀之勝亦我也。

translations.literal: The victor at Dachangyuan was I, the victor at Weizhou was also I, and the victor at Daohuigu was also I.
translations.idiomatic: I won at Dachangyuan. I won at Weizhou. I won at Daohuigu.

sentences.zh: 我死亂軍中，人將謂我負國家，今日明白死，天下必有知我者。

translations.literal: If I die in the chaos of the army, people will say I betrayed the state; today I die openly, and there will surely be those in the realm who know me.
translations.idiomatic: If I die in this rout, men will say I betrayed my country. Today I die openly, and there will be those in the realm who know what I was.

sentences.zh: 」時欲其降，斫足脛折不為屈，豁口吻至耳，噀血而呼，至死不絕。

translations.literal: " They wished him to surrender; they hacked his shins until they broke, yet he would not yield; they split his mouth to the ear, spat blood, and shouted — until death he did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: " They wanted his surrender. They hacked his shins until they broke, yet he would not yield. They split his mouth to the ear; he spat blood and shouted until he died without ceasing.

sentences.zh: 大將義之，酹以馬湩，祝曰：「好男子，他日再生，當令我得之。

translations.literal: The great general honored his righteousness, poured libation with kumiss, and prayed, "A fine man — if he is born again another day, may I obtain him.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy commander admired his spirit, poured kumiss in libation, and prayed, "A fine man — if he is born again, may I win him for my own.

sentences.zh: 」時年四十一。

translations.literal: " He was then forty-one.
translations.idiomatic: " He was forty-one years old.

sentences.zh: 是年六月，詔贈鎮南軍節度使，塑像褒忠廟，勒石紀其忠烈。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of that year, an edict posthumously granted him Military Commissioner of the Army That Pacifies the South; a statue was placed in the Temple of Commended Loyalty, and stone was carved to record his loyal valor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of that year an edict posthumously made him military commissioner of the Army That Pacifies the South. A statue was placed in the Temple of Commended Loyalty, and stone was carved to record his loyal valor.

sentences.zh: 斜烈名鼎，字國器，畢里海世襲猛安。

translations.literal: Xielie's name was Ding, courtesy name Guoqi, hereditary meng'an of Bilihai.
translations.idiomatic: Xielie, whose name was Ding and courtesy name Guoqi, held the hereditary meng'an of Bilihai.

sentences.zh: 年二十，以善戰知名。

translations.literal: At twenty he was known for skill in battle.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he was already famed for prowess in battle.

sentences.zh: 自壽、泗元帥轉安平都尉，鎮商州，威望甚重，敬賢下士，有古賢將之風。

translations.literal: From the Shou-Si marshal he was transferred to Anping Commandant, garrisoned Shangzhou, and his prestige was very great; he honored the worthy and humbled himself before scholars, with the air of ancient worthy generals.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred from the Shou-Si command to commandant of Anping, he garrisoned Shangzhou with great prestige, honoring the worthy and humbling himself before scholars in the manner of the great generals of old.

sentences.zh: 初至商州，一日搜伏，于大竹林中得歐陽修子孫，問而知之，並其族屬鄉里三千餘人皆縱遣之。

translations.literal: When he first arrived at Shangzhou, one day in searching hidden persons in a great bamboo grove he found descendants of Ouyang Xiu; on inquiry he learned who they were, and together with their clansmen and fellow townsmen, more than three thousand in all, he released and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he reached Shangzhou, a search for hidden persons in a great bamboo grove turned up descendants of Ouyang Xiu. Once he learned who they were, he released them together with more than three thousand clansmen and fellow townsmen.

sentences.zh: 楊沃衍

translations.literal: Yang Woyan
translations.idiomatic: Yang Woyan

sentences.zh: 楊沃衍，一名斡烈，賜姓兀林答，朔州靜邊官莊人，本屬唐括迪剌部族。

translations.literal: Yang Woyan, also named Wolie, was granted the surname Ulin'da, a native of Jingbian Official Estate in Shuozhou, originally of the Tangut Dila tribal group.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Woyan, also called Wolie, was granted the surname Ulin'da. He came from the Jingbian Official Estate in Shuozhou and was originally of the Tangut Dila tribe.

sentences.zh: 少嘗為北邊屯田小吏，會大元兵入境，朝命徙唐括族內地，沃衍留不徙，率本部族願從者入保朔州南山茶杞溝，有眾數千，推沃衍為招撫使，號其溝曰府，故殘破鎮縣徒黨日集，官軍不能制。

translations.literal: In youth he had served as a minor clerk in northern frontier colony fields; when the Great Yuan army entered the borders, the court ordered the Tangut tribes moved inland; Woyan remained and did not move, leading those of his tribal group who wished to follow into refuge in Chaqi Ravine in the southern mountains of Shuozhou, with several thousand followers; they made Woyan Pacification Commissioner and called his ravine a prefecture; as ruined towns and counties daily gathered displaced bands, government troops could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he had served as a minor clerk on the northern frontier colony fields. When the armies of the Great Yuan crossed the border, the court ordered the Tangut tribes moved inland. Woyan stayed behind, leading willing clansmen into Chaqi Ravine in the southern mountains of Shuozhou. Several thousand men gathered, made him pacification commissioner, and called his ravine a prefecture. As ruined towns and counties sent more displaced bands every day, government troops could not control them.

sentences.zh: 又與大兵戰，連獲小捷，及乏食，遂行剽劫。

translations.literal: He also fought the great army and won small victories in succession; when food ran short, he then turned to raiding.
translations.idiomatic: He fought the enemy repeatedly and won a string of small victories, but when food ran short he turned to raiding.

sentences.zh: 官軍捕之，拒戰不下，轉走寧、隩、武、朔、甯邊諸州，民以為病。

translations.literal: Government troops pursued him; he resisted and they could not take him, shifting through Ning, You, Wu, Shuo, and Ningbian prefectures, and the people regarded him as a scourge.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops pursued him, but he resisted and could not be taken, moving through Ning, You, Wu, Shuo, and Ningbian. The people suffered under him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣人招之，沃衍即以眾來歸。

translations.literal: The court sent men to summon him, and Woyan came over at once with his followers.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent envoys to summon him, and Woyan came over at once with his followers.

sentences.zh: 時宣宗適南遷，次淇門，聞之甚喜，遂以為武州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xuanzong was just moving the capital south and had halted at Qimen; on hearing this he was greatly pleased and appointed him prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong was then moving the capital south and had halted at Qimen. Delighted at the news, he appointed Woyan prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 武州屢經殘毀，沃衍入州未幾，而大兵來攻，死戰二十七晝夜不能拔，乃退，時貞祐二年二月也。

translations.literal: Wuzhou had been ravaged repeatedly; Woyan had not long entered the prefecture when the great army came to attack; he fought to the death for twenty-seven days and nights and they could not take it, then they withdrew — this was in the second month of the second year of Zhenyou.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou had been ravaged again and again. Woyan had scarcely taken office when the enemy attacked. He fought to the death for twenty-seven days and nights until they could not take the city and withdrew. This was in the second month of the second year of Zhenyou.

sentences.zh: 既而朝廷以武州終不可守，令沃衍遷其軍民駐岢嵐州，以武州功擢為本州防禦使。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the court judged that Wuzhou could in the end not be held and ordered Woyan to move his soldiers and civilians to garrison at Kelan Prefecture; for his merit at Wuzhou he was promoted to defense commissioner of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon decided Wuzhou could not be held long term and ordered Woyan to move his soldiers and civilians to Kelan. For his defense of Wuzhou he was promoted to defense commissioner of Kelan.

sentences.zh: 俄升岢嵐為節鎮，以沃衍為節度使，仍詔諭曰：「卿于國盡忠，累有勞績。

translations.literal: Before long Kelan was raised to a military commission, with Woyan as military commissioner; an edict still instructed him, saying, "You have been utterly loyal to the state and have repeatedly achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: Kelan was soon raised to a military commission, with Woyan as its commissioner. An edict told him, "You have served the state with utter loyalty and won repeated merit.

sentences.zh: 今特升三品，恩亦厚矣，其益勵忠勤，與宣撫司輯睦以安軍民。

translations.literal: Now you are specially promoted three ranks; the favor is already generous — exert yourself further in loyalty and diligence, and work in harmony with the Pacification Commission to settle soldiers and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: You are now specially promoted three ranks — a generous favor. Press on in loyalty and diligence, and work in harmony with the Pacification Commission to settle soldiers and civilians.

sentences.zh: 」沃衍自奉詔即以身許國，曰：「為人不死王事而死於家，非大丈夫也。」

translations.literal: " From the time he received the edict Woyan devoted his person to the state, saying, "For a man not to die in the king's service but to die at home is not the act of a great man."
translations.idiomatic: " From the moment he received the edict, Woyan pledged his life to the state, saying, "For a man to die at home rather than in the king's service is not the act of a great man."

sentences.zh: 三年，奉旨屯涇、邠、隴三州，沃衍分其軍九千人為十翼五都統，親統者十之四。

translations.literal: In the third year, by imperial order he garrisoned the three prefectures of Jing, Bin, and Long; Woyan divided his army of nine thousand into ten wings and five commanders-in-chief, personally commanding four-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was ordered to garrison Jing, Bin, and Long. Woyan divided his nine thousand men into ten wings under five commanders-in-chief, keeping four-tenths under his own command.

sentences.zh: 是冬，西夏四萬餘騎圍定西州，元帥右都監完顏賽不以沃衍提控軍事，率兵與夏人戰，斬首幾二千，生擒數十人，獲馬八百餘匹，器械稱是，餘悉遁去。

translations.literal: That winter, Xixia with more than forty thousand horsemen besieged Dingxi Prefecture; the Marshal's Right Overseer Wanyan Saibu placed Woyan in control of military affairs; he led troops to fight the Xia people, beheading nearly two thousand, capturing several tens alive, taking more than eight hundred horses, and weapons in proportion; the rest all fled.
translations.idiomatic: That winter more than forty thousand Xia horsemen besieged Dingxi. Marshal's right overseer Wanyan Saibu placed Woyan in command. He met the Xia in battle, beheaded nearly two thousand, took several dozen prisoners, seized more than eight hundred horses and a full complement of weapons, and drove the rest off.

sentences.zh: 詔陝西行省視功官賞之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat to review his merit and grant official rewards.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat to review his merit and grant rewards.

sentences.zh: 元光元年正月，遙授中京留守。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Yuanguang, he was appointed in absentia as defender of the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Yuanguang he was appointed in absentia defender of the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 六月，進拜元帥右監軍，仍世襲納古胡裏愛必剌謀克。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he was advanced to Marshal's Right Overseer of the Army, still with hereditary mouke of Naguhulai Aibila.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was promoted to marshal's right overseer of the army, retaining hereditary mouke status of Naguhulai Aibila.

sentences.zh: 二年春，北兵遊騎數百掠延安而南，沃衍率兵追之，戰於野豬嶺，獲四人而還。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year, several hundred northern raiding horsemen plundered Yan'an and went south; Woyan led troops in pursuit and fought at Wild Boar Ridge, capturing four men and returning.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year several hundred northern raiders plundered Yan'an and moved south. Woyan pursued, fought at Wild Boar Ridge, took four prisoners, and returned.

sentences.zh: 俄而，兵大至，駐德安寨，複擊走之。

translations.literal: Before long a large force arrived and encamped at De'an Stockade; he again attacked and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a larger force arrived and encamped at De'an Stockade. He attacked again and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 未幾，大兵攻鳳翔還，道出保安，沃衍遣提控完顏查剌破于石樓臺，前後獲馬二百、符印數十。

translations.literal: Before long the great army attacked Fengxiang and returned; their route passed Bao'an; Woyan sent military controller Wanyan Zhala to defeat them at Shilou Terrace, in all taking two hundred horses and several tens of tallies and seals.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the main army attacked Fengxiang and withdrew by way of Bao'an. Woyan sent military controller Wanyan Zhala to defeat them at Shilou Terrace, capturing two hundred horses and several dozen tallies and seals.

sentences.zh: 詔有司論賞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to deliberate rewards.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the relevant offices to deliberate his reward.

sentences.zh: 初，聞野豬嶺有兵，沃衍約陀滿胡土門以步軍會戰。

translations.literal: Earlier, on hearing there were troops at Wild Boar Ridge, Woyan had arranged with Tuoman Hutumen to join battle with infantry.
translations.idiomatic: When he first heard of troops at Wild Boar Ridge, Woyan had arranged with Tuoman Hutumen to join him with infantry.

sentences.zh: 胡土門宿將，常輕沃衍，至是失期。

translations.literal: Hutumen was a veteran general and had always looked down on Woyan; this time he missed the rendezvous.
translations.idiomatic: Hutumen was a veteran who had always looked down on Woyan. This time he missed the rendezvous.

sentences.zh: 沃衍戰還，會諸將欲斬胡土門，諸將哀請乃釋之。

translations.literal: When Woyan returned from battle he gathered the generals and wished to execute Hutumen; the generals pleaded piteously and only then was he released.
translations.idiomatic: When Woyan returned from battle he gathered the generals and wished to execute Hutumen. They pleaded piteously until he relented.

sentences.zh: 時大兵聲勢益振，陝西行省檄沃衍清野，不從，曰；

translations.literal: At that time the great army's momentum grew ever stronger; the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat ordered Woyan to clear the countryside, but he did not comply, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The enemy's momentum was growing. The Shaanxi Branch Secretariat ordered Woyan to clear the countryside. He refused, saying:

sentences.zh: 「我若清野，明年民何所得食？

translations.literal: "If I clear the countryside, what will the people have to eat next year?
translations.idiomatic: "If I clear the countryside, what will the people eat next year?

sentences.zh: 」遂隔大澗持勢使民畢麥事。

translations.literal: " He then held position across the great ravine and had the people complete the wheat harvest.
translations.idiomatic: " He held position across the great ravine and let the people finish the wheat harvest.

sentences.zh: 正大二年，進拜元帥左監軍，遙領中京留守。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengda he was advanced to Marshal's Left Overseer of the Army and held in absentia the post of defender of the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengda he was promoted to marshal's left overseer of the army and continued to hold the absentee post of defender of the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 八年冬，平章合達、參政蒲阿由鄧州而西，沃衍自豐陽川遇於五朵山下，問禹山之戰如何，合達曰：「我軍雖勝，而大兵已散漫趨京師矣。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eighth year, Grand Councilor Heda and Administrative Assistant Pu'a came west from Dengzhou. Woyan came from Fengyang River and they met at the foot of Mount Wuduo. He asked how the battle at Yushan had gone. Heda said: "Although our army was victorious, the great army had already scattered in disorder and rushed toward the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That winter in the eighth year, Grand Councilor Heda and Administrative Assistant Pu'a marched west from Dengzhou. Woyan came from Fengyang River and met them at the foot of Mount Wuduo. He asked how the battle at Yushan had gone. Heda said, "We won, but the enemy army had already scattered and was rushing toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 」沃衍憤雲：「平章、參政蒙國厚恩，握兵柄，失事機，不能戰禦，乃縱兵深入，尚何言耶！」

translations.literal: " Woyan said angrily: "Grand Councilor and Administrative Assistant, you have received the state's deep favor and hold military power. You missed the critical moment, could not fight and defend, yet let troops advance deeply — what more is there to say!"
translations.idiomatic: " Woyan said angrily, "Grand Councilor, Administrative Assistant — you enjoyed the state's deep favor and held military command. You missed your chance, failed to fight and defend, and let the enemy advance unchecked. What more is there to say!"

sentences.zh: 三峰山之敗，沃衍走鈞州。

translations.literal: After the defeat at Mount Sanfeng, Woyan fled to Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Mount Sanfeng, Woyan fled to Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 其部曲白留奴、呆劉勝既降，請于大帥，願入鈞招沃衍。

translations.literal: His retainers Bailiunu and Dull Liu Sheng having already surrendered, requested of the chief commander that they be allowed to enter Jun to summon Woyan to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: His retainers Bailiunu and Dull Liu Sheng had already surrendered. They asked the chief commander for permission to enter Junzhou and persuade Woyan to surrender.

sentences.zh: 大帥質留奴，令勝入鈞見沃衍，道大帥意，降則當授大官。

translations.literal: The chief commander took Bailiunu as hostage and sent Sheng into Jun to see Woyan, conveying the commander's intention that if he surrendered he would be granted high office.
translations.idiomatic: The chief commander held Bailiunu hostage and sent Liu Sheng into Junzhou to see Woyan, conveying the commander's offer: surrender and he would receive high office.

sentences.zh: 沃衍善言慰撫之，使前，拔劍斫之，曰：「我起身細微，蒙國大恩，汝欲以此汙我耶！

translations.literal: Woyan spoke kindly words to comfort and reassure him, had him approach, then drew his sword and hacked at him, saying: "I rose from humble beginnings and received the state's great grace — do you wish to stain me with this!
translations.idiomatic: Woyan spoke kindly to reassure him and had him come forward — then drew his sword and cut him down. "I rose from humble origins and received the state's great grace," he said. "Do you mean to stain me with this?

sentences.zh: 」遂遺語部曲後事，望汴京拜且哭曰：「無面目見朝廷，惟有一死耳。

translations.literal: " He then left instructions to his retainers on final affairs, faced Bianjing, bowed and wept, saying: "I have no face to see the court — death is all that remains.
translations.idiomatic: " He then entrusted final affairs to his retainers, turned toward Bianjing, bowed, and wept. "I have no face left to meet the court," he said. "There is nothing for me but death.

sentences.zh: 」即自縊。

translations.literal: " He then hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: " He hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 部曲舉火並所寓屋焚之，從死者十余人。

translations.literal: His retainers set fire and burned the house where he lodged; more than ten died with him.
translations.idiomatic: His retainers set fire and burned the house where he was staying. More than ten died with him.

sentences.zh: 沃衍死時年五十二。

translations.literal: When Woyan died he was fifty-two years old.
translations.idiomatic: Woyan was fifty-two when he died.

sentences.zh: 初，大兵破西夏，長驅而至，關輔千里皆洶洶不安，雖智者亦無如之何。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the great army destroyed Western Xia and came in a long drive, for a thousand li across Guanfu all was in tumultuous unrest, and even the wise could do nothing about it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the enemy swept through Western Xia and rode hard eastward, unrest spread for a thousand li across the Guanzhong region. Even the wisest could see no remedy.

sentences.zh: 沃衍與其部將劉興哥者率兵往來邠、隴間，屢戰屢勝，故大軍猝不能東下。

translations.literal: Woyan and his subordinate general Liu Xingge led troops back and forth between Bin and Long, fighting repeatedly and winning repeatedly; thus the great army could not suddenly advance eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Woyan and his subordinate Liu Xingge led troops between Bin and Long, winning battle after battle — so the enemy could not push east at once.

sentences.zh: 興哥，鳳翔虢縣人，起於群盜，人呼曰「熱劉」。

translations.literal: Xingge was a native of Guo County in Fengxiang, rose from bandit gangs; people called him "Hot Liu."
translations.idiomatic: Xingge came from Guo County in Fengxiang. He had risen from bandit bands, and people called him "Hot Liu."

sentences.zh: 後於清化戰死，大兵至酹酒以吊，西州耆老語之。

translations.literal: Later he died in battle at Qinghua; when the great army arrived they poured libations to mourn him, and the elders of the western prefectures spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: He later died fighting at Qinghua. When the enemy army arrived they poured wine in mourning, and the elders of the western prefectures spoke of his death.

sentences.zh: 至為泣下。

translations.literal: They wept to the point of shedding tears.
translations.idiomatic: They wept.

sentences.zh: 烏古論黑漢

translations.literal: Wugulun Heihan
translations.idiomatic: Wugulun Heihan

sentences.zh: 烏古論黑漢，初以親軍入仕，嘗為唐、鄧元帥府把軍官。

translations.literal: Wugulun Heihan first entered service as a personal guard soldier and once served as a garrison officer of the Tang-Deng Marshal's Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Wugulun Heihan entered service as an imperial guardsman and had once served as a garrison officer under the Tang-Deng marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 天興二年，唐州刺史內族斜魯病卒，鄧州總帥府以蒲察都尉權唐州事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianxing, Tangzhou Prefect, imperial clansman Xielu, died of illness. The Dengzhou supreme commander's headquarters appointed Captain Pucha to act as prefect of Tangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianxing, Tang Prefect Xielu of the imperial clan died of illness. The Dengzhou supreme commander's headquarters put Captain Pucha in charge of Tang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宋軍兩來圍唐，又唐之糧多為鄧州所取，以故乏食。

translations.literal: Song troops twice came to besiege Tang, and moreover much of Tang's grain had been taken by Dengzhou; for this reason they lacked food.
translations.idiomatic: Song forces twice besieged Tang Prefecture, and much of its grain had been taken by Dengzhou — so the city went hungry.

sentences.zh: 六月，遣萬戶夾穀定住入歸德，奏請軍糧，不報。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he sent Commander Jiagu Dingzhu to enter Guide to memorialize and request military grain; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he sent Commander Jiagu Dingzhu to Guide to request military grain from the court. No reply came.

sentences.zh: 七月，鎮防軍馮總領、甄改住為變，殺蒲察都尉。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, garrison troops Commandant Feng and Zhen Gaizhu mutinied and killed Captain Pucha.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, garrison commanders Feng and Zhen Gaizhu mutinied and killed Captain Pucha.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷道梗，帥府承制以黑漢權刺史行帥府事。

translations.literal: At that time the roads to court were blocked; the commander's headquarters issued orders on its own authority appointing Heihan acting prefect to conduct the headquarters' affairs.
translations.idiomatic: With the roads to court cut off, the commander's headquarters appointed Heihan acting prefect and had him run headquarters affairs.

sentences.zh: 既而鎮防軍有歸宋之謀，時裕州大成山聶都統一軍五百人在州，獨不欲歸宋，與鎮防軍為敵，鎮防不能勝，棄老幼奔棗陽，宋人以故知唐之虛實。

translations.literal: Before long the garrison troops plotted to surrender to Song. At that time Commander Nie of Dacheng Mountain in Yuzhou had five hundred troops in the prefecture who alone did not wish to surrender to Song. They became enemies of the garrison troops; the garrison could not prevail, abandoned old and young and fled to Zaoyang, and the Song people thereby learned Tang's true situation.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the garrison troops plotted to defect to Song. Commander Nie of Dacheng Mountain in Yuzhou had five hundred men in the prefecture who refused to join them. They fought the garrison and held their ground; the garrison could not defeat them and fled to Zaoyang with their dependents, letting the Song learn how weak Tang really was.

sentences.zh: 會鄧帥移剌瑗以城叛歸於宋，遺書招黑漢，黑漢殺其使者不報。

translations.literal: It happened that the Deng commander Yila Yuan rebelled with the city and surrendered to Song; he sent a letter summoning Heihan, and Heihan killed his messenger and gave no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Deng Commander Yila Yuan betrayed the city and surrendered to Song. He sent a letter inviting Heihan to join him. Heihan killed the messenger and refused.

sentences.zh: 宋王安撫率兵攻唐，鄂司王太尉繼至，攻益急。

translations.literal: Song Commissioner Wang led troops to attack Tang; Grand Marshal Wang of the E Department arrived next, and the attack grew fiercer still.
translations.idiomatic: Song Commissioner Wang led troops against Tang Prefecture. Grand Marshal Wang of the E Circuit arrived in support, and the assault intensified.

sentences.zh: 黑漢聞哀宗遷蔡，遣人求救，上命權參政兀林答胡土將兵以往。

translations.literal: Heihan heard that Emperor Aizong had moved to Cai and sent someone to plead for rescue; the emperor ordered Acting Administrative Assistant Ulin'da Hutu to lead troops there.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Emperor Aizong had moved to Cai, Heihan sent messengers begging for relief. The emperor ordered Acting Administrative Assistant Ulin'da Hutu to march to his aid.

sentences.zh: 宋人設伏，縱其半入城，邀擊之，胡土大敗，僅存三十騎以還。

translations.literal: The Song set an ambush, let half his force enter the city, then intercepted and struck; Hutu suffered a great defeat and returned with only thirty horsemen surviving.
translations.idiomatic: The Song laid an ambush, let half his force enter the city, then struck. Hutu was routed and returned with only thirty horsemen left.

sentences.zh: 城中糧盡，人相食，黑漢殺其愛妾啖士，士爭殺其妻子。

translations.literal: Grain in the city was exhausted and people ate one another; Heihan killed his beloved concubine to feed the troops, and the soldiers competed in killing their wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: When the city's grain ran out, people ate one another. Heihan killed his beloved concubine to feed his men. Soldiers began killing their own wives and children.

sentences.zh: 官屢聚議欲降，黑漢與聶都統執議益堅，馮總領乃私出城與王安撫會飲，約明日宋軍入城。

translations.literal: Officials repeatedly gathered to discuss surrender; Heihan and Commander Nie held to their position ever more firmly. Commandant Feng then privately left the city to meet Commissioner Wang for drink, agreeing that the Song army would enter the city the next day.
translations.idiomatic: Officials repeatedly met to discuss surrender, but Heihan and Commander Nie held firm. Commandant Feng slipped out to drink with Commissioner Wang and arranged for the Song to enter the city the next day.

sentences.zh: 馮歸，宋軍不得入，聶都統請馮議事，即坐中斬之。

translations.literal: Feng returned; the Song army could not enter. Commander Nie invited Feng to discuss affairs and cut him down right there where they sat.
translations.idiomatic: Feng returned before the Song could enter. Commander Nie summoned him to discuss business and executed him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 及其黨皆死。

translations.literal: He and his faction all died.
translations.idiomatic: He and his followers were all killed.

sentences.zh: 總領趙醜兒者初與馮同謀，內不自安，開西門納宋軍。

translations.literal: Commandant Zhao Chou'er, who had originally plotted with Feng, felt uneasy within himself and opened the west gate to admit the Song army.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Zhao Chou'er, Feng's co-conspirator, lost his nerve and opened the west gate to the Song.

sentences.zh: 黑漢率大成山軍巷戰，自辰至午，宋軍大敗而出，殺傷無數。

translations.literal: Heihan led the Dacheng Mountain army in street fighting from the chen hour to the wu hour; the Song army suffered a great defeat and retreated, with countless killed and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Heihan led the Dacheng Mountain troops in street fighting from morning until midday. The Song were routed with countless casualties.

sentences.zh: 宋人城下大呼趙醜兒，約並力殺大成山軍。

translations.literal: Below the wall the Song shouted loudly for Zhao Chou'er, arranging together to kill the Dacheng Mountain army.
translations.idiomatic: Below the walls the Song shouted for Zhao Chou'er, urging him to join them in destroying the Dacheng Mountain troops.

sentences.zh: 大成軍敗，宋人獲黑漢，脅使降，黑漢不屈，為所殺。

translations.literal: The Dacheng army was defeated; the Song captured Heihan, coerced him to surrender; Heihan would not submit and was killed by them.
translations.idiomatic: The Dacheng Mountain force was beaten. The Song captured Heihan and pressed him to surrender. He refused and was killed.

sentences.zh: 其得脫走者十餘人，總領移剌望軍、女奚烈軍、醜兒走蔡州，皆得遷賞，後俱死於甲午之難。

translations.literal: More than ten who escaped by fleeing survived; Commandants Yila Wangjun, Nuxilie Jun, and Chou'er fled to Caizhou, all received promoted rewards, and later all died in the disaster of the jiawu year.
translations.idiomatic: A dozen or so men escaped. Commandants Yila Wangjun, Nuxilie Jun, and Chou'er fled to Caizhou and were all promoted and rewarded — only to die later in the jiawu disaster.

sentences.zh: 陀滿胡土門

translations.literal: Tuoman Hutumen
translations.idiomatic: Tuoman Hutumen

sentences.zh: 陀滿胡土門，字子秀，策論進士也。

translations.literal: Tuoman Hutumen, courtesy name Zixiu, was a jinshi by policy essay examination.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoman Hutumen, courtesy name Zixiu, had passed the jinshi examination in policy essays.

sentences.zh: 累官翰林待制。

translations.literal: Through successive appointments he reached Hanlin Attendant Drafting.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Hanlin Attendant Drafting.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，遷知中山府。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou he was transferred to administer Zhongshan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyou he was appointed prefect of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 三年，改知臨洮府、兼本路兵馬都總管。

translations.literal: In the third year he was changed to administer Lin'tao Prefecture and concurrently serve as overall commander of the route's military forces.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became prefect of Lin'tao and concurrent overall commander of the circuit's forces.

sentences.zh: 叛賊蘭州程陳僧等誘夏人入寇，圍臨洮凡半月，城中兵數千而粟且不支，眾皆危之。

translations.literal: Rebel bandits Cheng Chenseng of Lanzhou and others induced Xia people to invade; they besieged Lin'tao for half a month altogether. Within the city were several thousand troops but grain would not last; everyone regarded the situation as perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels such as Cheng Chenseng of Lanzhou induced the Xia to raid. They besieged Lin'tao for half a month. The city had several thousand troops but grain was running out, and morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 胡土門日為開諭逆順禍福，皆自奮。

translations.literal: Hutumen daily expounded on the fortunes and disasters of loyalty and rebellion, and all roused themselves to exertion.
translations.idiomatic: Hutumen daily explained the rewards of loyalty and the cost of treason, and the men rallied.

sentences.zh: 因捕其黨欲為內應者二十人，斬之，擲首城外。

translations.literal: Thereupon he captured twenty of their party who wished to serve as inside collaborators, beheaded them, and threw the heads outside the wall.
translations.idiomatic: He seized twenty men plotting to open the gates from within, beheaded them, and hurled their heads over the wall.

sentences.zh: 賊四面來攻，乃夜出襲賊壘，夏兵大亂，金軍乘之，遂大捷，夏人遁去。

translations.literal: The bandits attacked from all four sides; he then sallied out at night to strike their camp; Xia troops fell into great disorder; Jin troops pressed the advantage and achieved a great victory; the Xia people fled away.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy attacked from every side, he sallied out at night and struck their camp. The Xia broke in confusion; the Jin pressed the advantage and won a great victory, and the raiders fled.

sentences.zh: 四年，知河中府事，權河東南路宣撫副使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he governed Hezhong Prefecture affairs and held in authority the deputy military commissioner of Hedong South Route.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he governed Hezhong and served as deputy military commissioner of the Hedong South Circuit.

sentences.zh: 十月，進元帥右監軍、兼前職。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was advanced to Marshal's Right Overseer of the Army, concurrently keeping his former posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was promoted to marshal's right overseer of the army while keeping his other posts.

sentences.zh: 興定二年，為絳陽軍節度使、兼絳州管內觀察使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xingding he served as military governor of Jiangyang Army and concurrently observation commissioner within Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xingding he became military governor of Jiangyang Army and concurrent observation commissioner of Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十月，遷元帥左監軍、行元帥府事、兼知晉安府、河東南路兵馬都總管。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was transferred to Marshal's Left Overseer of the Army, acting marshal's headquarters affairs, concurrently administering Jin'an Prefecture, and overall commander of Hedong South Route military forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was made marshal's left overseer of the army, acting head of the marshal's headquarters, prefect of Jin'an, and overall commander of the Hedong South Circuit.

sentences.zh: 於是，修城池，繕甲兵，積芻糧，以備戰守。

translations.literal: Thereupon he repaired city walls and moats, readied armor and weapons, accumulated fodder and grain, to prepare for warfare and defense.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired the walls, sharpened arms, and stockpiled fodder and grain to prepare for siege and defense.

sentences.zh: 民不悅，行省胥鼎聞之，遺以書曰：「元帥始鎮河中，惠愛在民，移ＩＭ晉安，遠近忻仰。

translations.literal: The people were displeased; Branch Secretariat Chief Xu Ding heard of it and sent him a letter saying: "When the Marshal first commanded at Hezhong, his kindness and love rested on the people; when he moved his command to Jin'an, near and far rejoiced and looked up to him.
translations.idiomatic: The people were unhappy. Branch Secretariat Chief Xu Ding heard of it and wrote: "When you first held command at Hezhong, the people felt your kindness. When you moved your command to Jin'an, men near and far rejoiced in you.

sentences.zh: 去歲兵入，平陽不守，河東保完者惟絳而已。

translations.literal: Last year when troops entered, Pingyang could not be held; in Hedong what remained intact was only Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Last year when the enemy invaded, Pingyang fell. Of all Hedong, only Jiang Prefecture held firm.

sentences.zh: 蓋公坐籌制勝，威德素著，故不動聲氣以至無虞也。

translations.literal: This was because the lord sat and planned to overcome the enemy; his authority and virtue had long been established, so without stirring breath or voice he achieved freedom from worry.
translations.idiomatic: You won through careful planning; your authority and virtue were already famed — so you kept the peace without raising an alarm.

sentences.zh: 邇來傳聞，治政太剛，科征太重，鼎切憂之。

translations.literal: Recently I have heard reports that governance is too harsh, and tax levies too heavy; Ding is deeply worried about this.
translations.idiomatic: Lately I hear your rule has grown too harsh and your levies too heavy. This troubles me deeply.

sentences.zh: 古人有言，禦下不寬則人多懼禍，用人有疑則士不盡心。

translations.literal: The ancients had a saying: if one is not lenient in governing subordinates, then many people will fear calamity; if one has doubts in employing men, then officers will not give their full hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: rule your subordinates too harshly and men will fear for their lives; doubt the men you employ and they will not give you their best.

sentences.zh: 況大兵在邇，鄰境已虛，小人易動，誠不可不慮也。

translations.literal: Moreover the great army is near, neighboring territories are already empty, petty men are easily moved — this truly cannot be left unconsidered.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy is near, neighboring territories lie stripped, and petty men are easily swayed. This must not be ignored.

sentences.zh: 願公以謙虛待下，忠孝結人，明賞罰，平賦稅，上以分聖主宵旰之憂，下以為河東長城之托。

translations.literal: I hope the lord will treat subordinates with modest humility, bind men with loyalty and filial piety, clarify rewards and punishments, balance taxes and levies — above to share the sacred lord's anxiety through sleepless nights, below to serve as the trust of Hedong's Great Wall.
translations.idiomatic: Treat your men with humility. Win them through loyalty and fairness. Make rewards and punishments clear and keep taxes level — easing the emperor's sleepless worry above and standing as Hedong's bulwark below.

sentences.zh: 」胡土門得書，懼民不從且或生變，乃上言：「臣本瑣材，猥膺重寄，方將治隍碑、積芻糧為捍禦之計，而小民難與慮始，以臣政令頗急，皆有怨言，遂貽行省之憂。

translations.literal: " Hutumen received the letter, feared the people would not follow and might produce revolt, and thus memorialized: "Your subject is originally a petty talent who unworthily received heavy trust. I was just about to repair walls and moats and accumulate fodder and grain for plans of defense, but common folk are hard to consult at the beginning of affairs. Because my government orders were rather urgent, all had complaint words, and thus I caused the Branch Secretariat's worry.
translations.idiomatic: " Hutumen received the letter, feared the people would not obey and might revolt, and memorialized: "I am a man of little talent who unworthily bears heavy responsibility. I have been repairing walls and moats and stockpiling grain for defense, but common people resist plans before they see results. My orders have been strict, grumbling has spread, and I have troubled the Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 自聞訓諭，措身無所，內自悛悔，外加寬撫，庶幾少慰眾心。

translations.literal: Since hearing your instructive admonition I have had nowhere to place myself; inwardly I repent and reform, outwardly I add lenient reassurance — hoping somewhat to soothe the hearts of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Since your admonition I have been at a loss. I repent inwardly and soften my rule outwardly, hoping to ease popular anger.

sentences.zh: 而近以朝命分軍過河，則又喧言帥臣不益兵保守，而反助河南，將棄我也。

translations.literal: Yet recently by court order troops were divided to cross the river, and again there was noisy talk that the commander would not augment troops to defend and hold, but rather was helping Henan and would abandon us.
translations.idiomatic: Then the court ordered troops sent across the river, and rumor spread that the commander would not reinforce the defense but was aiding Henan and meant to abandon us.

sentences.zh: 人心如此，恐一旦遂生他變。

translations.literal: Popular sentiment is thus; I fear that suddenly some other change will arise.
translations.idiomatic: Morale is this fragile. I fear a sudden uprising.

sentences.zh: 向者李革在平陽，人不安之，而革隱忍不言，以至於敗。

translations.literal: Formerly Li Ge was at Pingyang; the people were unsettled under him, yet Ge endured in silence without speaking, until it led to defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Ge was at Pingyang the people were restless, but he kept silent until disaster came.

sentences.zh: 臣實拙繆，無以服人，敢以鼎書上聞，惟朝廷圖之。

translations.literal: Your subject is truly clumsy and erroneous, unable to win men's obedience; I dare report Ding's letter to your attention — may the court consider it.
translations.idiomatic: I am too clumsy to command men's loyalty. I submit Chief Xu Ding's letter for the court's judgment.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷以鼎言，遣吏部尚書守顏閭山代之。

translations.literal: " The court, on account of Ding's words, dispatched Minister of Personnel Shou Yan Lüshan to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: " On Xu Ding's advice the court sent Minister of Personnel Shou Yan Lüshan to replace him.

sentences.zh: 或曰，胡土門欲以計去晉安，乃大興役，恣為殺戮，務失民心，故鼎言及之。

translations.literal: Some say Hutumen wished by stratagem to leave Jin'an; therefore he launched great corvée labor, indulged in killing at will, deliberately losing popular hearts — hence Ding's words touched on it.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Hutumen wanted to leave Jin'an by design — that he imposed heavy labor, killed freely, and deliberately alienated the people, which prompted Xu Ding's letter.

sentences.zh: 未幾，晉安失守，死者幾百萬人，遂失河東。

translations.literal: Before long Jin'an lost its defense; those who died numbered almost several million people; thereby Hedong was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jin'an fell. Nearly a million people died, and Hedong was lost.

sentences.zh: 三年八月，改太常卿、權簽樞密院事、知歸德府事。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year he was changed to Minister of Ceremonies, acting privy council signatory, and governing Guide Prefecture affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year he became Minister of Ceremonies, acting privy council signatory, and governor of Guide.

sentences.zh: 元光二年二月，坐上書不實，削一官。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Yuanguang, for submitting an inaccurate memorial he was reduced one rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Yuanguang 2 he was demoted one rank for filing a false report.

sentences.zh: 正大三年七月，複為臨洮府總管。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year of Zhengda he was restored as overall commander of Lin'tao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Zhengda 3 he was restored as overall commander of Lin'tao.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，城破被執，誘之降不應，使之跪不從，以刀亂斫其膝脛，終不為屈，遂殺之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year the city fell and he was captured; they enticed him to surrender but he did not respond; they made him kneel but he did not comply; with knives they hacked at his knees and shins in disorder; he ultimately would not submit and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year the city fell. Captured, he refused to surrender or kneel. They hacked at his knees and shins but could not break him, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔贈中京留守，立像褒忠廟，錄用其子孫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Defender of the Central Capital, erected his image in the Hall of Rewarding Loyalty, and enrolled and employed his sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the court posthumously made him Defender of the Central Capital, placed his portrait in the Hall of Rewarding Loyalty, and enrolled his descendants in office.

sentences.zh: 其妻烏古論氏亦死節，有傳。

translations.literal: His wife, Lady Wugulun, also died for principle; there is a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Lady Wugulun, also died loyal — she has her own biography.

sentences.zh: 姬汝作

translations.literal: Ji Ruzuo
translations.idiomatic: Ji Ruzuo

sentences.zh: 姬汝作，字欽之，汝陽人，全州節度副使端修之侄孫也。

translations.literal: Ji Ruzuo, courtesy name Qinzhi, was a native of Ruyang, the grand-nephew of Quanzhou Vice Military Governor Duanxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Ruzuo, courtesy name Qinzhi, came from Ruyang. He was the grand-nephew of Quanzhou Vice Military Governor Duanxiu.

sentences.zh: 父懋，以廕試部掾，轉尚書省令史。

translations.literal: His father Mao entered through yin privilege to test as a ministry clerk and was transferred to be a secretary of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mao entered service by yin privilege as a ministry clerk and became a secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 汝作讀書知義理，性豪宕，不拘細行，平日以才量稱。

translations.literal: Ruzuo read books and understood principle and reason; by nature he was bold and unrestrained, not bound by minor conduct; in ordinary times he was known for talent and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Ruzuo was well read and principled — bold and unconstrained by petty scruples, known for ability and breadth of mind.

sentences.zh: 正大末，避兵崧山，保鄉鄰數百家，眾以長事之。

translations.literal: Near the end of Zhengda he avoided troops at Song Mountain, protected several hundred households of neighboring villages, and the multitude treated him as elder leader.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Zhengda he took refuge on Song Mountain and sheltered several hundred neighboring households, who looked to him as their leader.

sentences.zh: 後徙居交牙山砦，會近侍局使烏古論四和撫諭西山，以便宜授汝作北山招撫使，佩銀符，遂遷入汝州。

translations.literal: Later he moved to dwell at Jiaoya Mountain Fortress. It happened that Palace Attendant Bureau Commissioner Wugulun Sihe pacified and reassured the western hills; by discretionary authority he appointed Ruzuo Pacification Commissioner of the Northern Hills, granted a silver tally, and thereupon he moved into Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later moved to Jiaoya Mountain Fortress. Palace Attendant Commissioner Wugulun Sihe was pacifying the western hills and appointed Ruzuo Pacification Commissioner of the Northern Hills with a silver tally. Ruzuo then moved into Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，汝州殘破之後，天興元年正月，同知宣徽院事張楷授防禦使，自汴率襄、郟縣土兵百餘人入青陽垛。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Ruzhou was ravaged and broken, in the first month of the first year of Tianxing, Associate Director of the Palace Attendant Bureau Zhang Kai was appointed Defense Commissioner; from Bian he led more than one hundred local troops of Xiang and Jia counties into Qingyang Rampart.
translations.idiomatic: After Ruzhou lay in ruins, in the first month of Tianxing 1 Zhang Kai, associate director of the Palace Attendant Bureau, was made defense commissioner. He led more than a hundred local troops from Xiang and Jia counties from Bian to Qingyang Rampart.

sentences.zh: 時呼延實者領青陽砦事。

translations.literal: At that time Huyan Shi was in charge of Qingyang Fortress affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Huyan Shi held Qingyang Fortress.

sentences.zh: 實趙城人，本楊沃衍部曲，以戰功至寶昌軍節度使，閒居汝之西山。

translations.literal: Shi was a native of Zhaocheng, originally a retainer of Yang Woyan; through battle merit he reached Military Governor of Baochang Army, living in retirement in the western hills of Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Shi came from Zhaocheng and had been a retainer of Yang Woyan. Battle honors had made him military governor of Baochang Army, and he was living in retirement in the western hills of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 楷自揣不能服眾，乃以州事托實，尋往鄧州從恆山公武仙。

translations.literal: Kai judged himself unable to command the multitude; thereupon he entrusted prefectural affairs to Shi, and soon went to Dengzhou to follow Duke of Hengshan Wu Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Kai knew he could not command the troops and turned prefectural affairs over to Shi, then went to Dengzhou to serve Duke of Hengshan Wu Xian.

sentences.zh: 後大元兵至，城破，殺數千人，乃許降，以張宣差者管州事。

translations.literal: Later when the Great Yuan army arrived, the city fell, several thousand were killed; only then was surrender permitted, and Zhang the Commissioner was put in charge of prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuan army arrived the city fell and thousands were killed. Surrender was accepted and Commissioner Zhang was put in charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三月，鈞州潰軍柳千戶者入州，張逃去，柳遂據之。

translations.literal: In the third month, routed troops from Junzhou — Commander Liu the thousand-household — entered the prefecture; Zhang fled; Liu thereupon seized it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month routed Junzhou troops under Commander Liu entered the city. Zhang fled and Liu seized the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未幾，城複破。

translations.literal: Before long the city again fell.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the city fell again.

sentences.zh: 及汝作至，北兵雖去，但空城爾。

translations.literal: When Ruzuo arrived, although the northern troops had left, it was only an empty city.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Ruzuo arrived the northern troops were gone — but the city was empty.

sentences.zh: 汝作招集散亡，複立市井，北兵屢招之不從，數戰互有勝負。

translations.literal: Ruzuo gathered and collected the scattered and lost, re-established markets and streets; the northern troops repeatedly summoned him but he did not comply; in several battles each side had victories and defeats.
translations.idiomatic: Ruzuo gathered the scattered population and rebuilt the market streets. The northern troops repeatedly summoned him; he refused. They fought several times with mixed results.

sentences.zh: 已而北兵複來攻，汝作親督士卒，以死拒之。

translations.literal: Before long the northern troops again came to attack; Ruzuo personally supervised the troops and resisted unto death.
translations.idiomatic: The northern army returned to attack. Ruzuo personally led his men and fought to the death to hold them off.

sentences.zh: 兵退，間道納奏，哀宗宣諭：「此州無險固可恃，汝乃能為國用命，今授以同知汝州防禦使，便宜從事。」

translations.literal: The troops retreated; through a bypath he submitted a memorial; Emperor Aizong issued an edict of encouragement: "This prefecture has no strong natural defenses to rely upon, yet you were able to give your life in service to the state; now I appoint you Associate Defense Commissioner of Ruzhou with discretionary authority."
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy withdrew he sent a memorial by secret route. Emperor Aizong proclaimed: "This prefecture has no natural defenses to speak of, yet you have served the state at mortal risk. I appoint you associate defense commissioner of Ruzhou with full discretionary powers."

sentences.zh: 是時，此州南通鄧州，西接洛陽，東則汴京，使傳所出，供億三面，傳通音耗。

translations.literal: At that time this prefecture connected south to Dengzhou, west adjoined Luoyang, east lay Bianjing — couriers and dispatches issued from it; supplies were furnished on three sides; couriers conveyed news and messages.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture linked south to Deng, west to Luoyang, and east to Bianjing. Couriers passed through it; it supplied three fronts and carried news in every direction.

sentences.zh: 然呼延實在青陽為總帥，忌汝作城守之功，不能相下，州事動為所制。

translations.literal: Yet Huyan Shi at Qingyang served as supreme commander; he envied Ruzuo's merit in holding the city in defense; neither could yield to the other; prefectural affairs were constantly controlled by him.
translations.idiomatic: But Huyan Shi, supreme commander at Qingyang, envied Ruzuo's success in holding the city. Neither would defer to the other, and Ruzuo's work was constantly blocked.

sentences.zh: 實欲遷州入山，謂他日必為大兵所破。

translations.literal: Shi wished to move the prefecture into the mountains, saying that one day it would surely be broken by the great army.
translations.idiomatic: Shi wanted to move the prefecture into the hills, convinced the enemy would eventually take the city.

sentences.zh: 汝作以為「倉中糧尚多，四面潰軍日至，此輩經百死，激之皆可用，朝廷倚我守此州，總帥乃欲棄之，何心哉。

translations.literal: Ruzuo considered: "Grain in the storehouses is still plentiful; routed troops arrive daily from all sides — these men have passed through a hundred deaths; rouse them and all can be used. The court relies on me to defend this prefecture, yet the supreme commander wishes to abandon it — what is in his heart!
translations.idiomatic: Ruzuo argued: "The granaries still hold grain. Routed troops arrive daily from every direction — men who have survived a hundred battles. Rouse them and they will fight. The court relies on us to hold this prefecture, and the supreme commander wants to abandon it — what kind of heart is that?

sentences.zh: 」讒間既行，有相圖之隙，詳議官楊鵬釋之曰：「外難未解而顧私忿。

translations.literal: " Slander and estrangement having taken effect, there was a gap for mutual plotting; Detail Review Officer Yang Peng explained: "External peril is not yet resolved yet you attend to private resentment.
translations.idiomatic: " Slander bred mistrust and the two men nearly came to blows. Detail Review Officer Yang Peng intervened: "The external enemy is not yet defeated, yet you indulge private grudges.

sentences.zh: 」語甚諄切。

translations.literal: " His words were very earnest and urgent.
translations.idiomatic: " He spoke with earnest urgency.

sentences.zh: 實乃還山，鵬因勸汝作納奏，乞死守此州，以堅軍民之心。

translations.literal: Shi thereupon returned to the mountains; Peng therefore urged Ruzuo to submit a memorial requesting to hold this prefecture to the death, to solidify the hearts of soldiers and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: Shi returned to the hills. Peng urged Ruzuo to memorialize the court, begging to defend the prefecture to the death and steady the hearts of troops and people.

sentences.zh: 其冬，戰於襄、郟，得馬百餘，士氣頗振，遂以汝作為總帥，不復與實相關矣。

translations.literal: That winter, fighting at Xiang and Jia, they obtained more than a hundred horses; troop morale was quite revived; thereupon Ruzuo was made supreme commander and no longer had connection with Shi.
translations.idiomatic: That winter they fought at Xiang and Jia and captured more than a hundred horses. Morale revived, and Ruzuo was made supreme commander — no longer answerable to Shi.

sentences.zh: 天興二年六月，哀宗在蔡州，遣使徵兵入援。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Tianxing, Emperor Aizong was at Caizhou and dispatched envoys to levy troops for relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Tianxing 2 Emperor Aizong, at Caizhou, sent envoys to call up troops for relief.

sentences.zh: 州人為邏騎所擾，農事盡廢，城中糧亦垂盡。

translations.literal: Prefecture people were harried by patrol cavalry; agricultural work was entirely abandoned; grain in the city was also nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Patrol cavalry harried the people; farming ceased; and the city's grain was nearly gone.

sentences.zh: 是月，中京破，部曲私議有脣亡之懼，計以城降，懼汝作，不敢言，乃以遷州入山白之。

translations.literal: That month the Central Capital fell; retainers privately discussed fear of lips perishing when teeth are cold; they plotted to surrender the city; fearing Ruzuo, they dared not speak openly, and therefore used moving the prefecture into the mountains to report it to him.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Central Capital fell. Ruzuo's retainers privately feared that when the lips are gone the teeth freeze — they plotted to surrender the city but dared not speak openly for fear of Ruzuo, and broached the idea of moving into the hills instead.

sentences.zh: 汝作怒曰：「吾家父祖食祿百年，今朝延又以州事帥職委我，吾生為金民，死為金鬼。

translations.literal: Ruzuo said angrily, "My forefathers have received salary from the state for a hundred years; now the court has entrusted me with both prefectural affairs and supreme command. Living I am a Jin subject; dead I shall be a Jin ghost.
translations.idiomatic: Ruzuo said in anger, "My forefathers have drawn salary from the state for a hundred years. The court has now entrusted me with both the prefecture and supreme command. Living, I am a subject of Jin; dead, I shall be a ghost of Jin.

sentences.zh: 汝輩欲避於山，非欲降乎？

translations.literal: You wish to flee to the mountains — is that not wishing to surrender?
translations.idiomatic: You want to flee to the mountains — is that not surrender in disguise?

sentences.zh: 有再言遷者吾必斬之。」

translations.literal: Whoever speaks of moving again, I shall surely behead."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever speaks of moving again, I shall behead."

sentences.zh: 八月，塔察將大兵攻蔡，經汝州。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Tacha led a great army to attack Cai and passed through Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Tacha led a great army against Cai and passed through Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 州人梁皋作亂，與故吏溫澤、王和七八人徑入州廨，汝作不為備，遂為所殺。

translations.literal: A townsman, Liang Gao, raised a disturbance; with former clerks Wen Ze, Wang He, and seven or eight others he went straight into the prefectural offices; Ruzuo was unprepared and was killed by them.
translations.idiomatic: A townsman named Liang Gao rebelled. With former clerks Wen Ze, Wang He, and seven or eight others he burst into the prefectural offices. Ruzuo was caught unprepared and killed.

sentences.zh: 時宣使石珪體究洛陽所以破及強伸死節事，以路阻，留汝州驛。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial commissioner Shi Gui was investigating how Luoyang had fallen and how Qiang Shen had died for his principles; the roads were blocked, and he stayed at the Ruzhou post station.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial commissioner Shi Gui was then investigating how Luoyang had fallen and how Qiang Shen had died for his principles. Blocked by the roads, he stayed at the Ruzhou post station.

sentences.zh: 梁皋既殺汝作，走告珪曰：「汝作私積糧斛，不恤軍民，眾怒殺之矣。

translations.literal: After Liang Gao had killed Ruzuo, he ran to tell Gui, saying, "Ruzuo privately hoarded grain and did not care for soldiers and civilians; the multitude in anger killed him.
translations.idiomatic: After killing Ruzuo, Liang Gao ran to Gui and said, "Ruzuo hoarded grain for himself and neglected soldiers and civilians. The people killed him in anger.

sentences.zh: 皋不圖汝作官職，惟宣使裁之。

translations.literal: Gao does not covet Ruzuo's office; let the imperial commissioner alone decide.
translations.idiomatic: I do not seek Ruzuo's office — let the imperial commissioner decide.

sentences.zh: 」圭懼，乃以皋權汝州防禦使、行帥府事。

translations.literal: " Gui was afraid and therefore made Gao acting defense commissioner of Ruzhou and head of the marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: " Gui, afraid, made Gao acting defense commissioner of Ruzhou and head of the marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 脫走入蔡，以皋殺汝作事聞。

translations.literal: He slipped away and fled to Cai, reporting that Gao had killed Ruzuo.
translations.idiomatic: He slipped away to Cai and reported that Gao had killed Ruzuo.

sentences.zh: 哀宗甚嗟惜之，遣近侍張天錫贈汝作昌武軍節度使，子孫世襲謀克，仍詔峴山帥呼延實、登封帥范真並力討皋。

translations.literal: Emperor Aizong deeply lamented this; he sent the inner attendant Zhang Tianxi to posthumously grant Ruzuo the post of Military Commissioner of the Changwu Army, with his descendants hereditary mouke, and still ordered the Xianshan commander Huyan Shi and the Dengfeng commander Fan Zhen to join forces to attack Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Aizong deeply lamented his death. He sent inner attendant Zhang Tianxi to posthumously make Ruzuo military commissioner of the Changwu Army, with hereditary mouke status for his descendants, and ordered Xianshan commander Huyan Shi and Dengfeng commander Fan Zhen to join forces against Gao.

sentences.zh: 天錫避峴山遠，先約範真，真以麾下李某者往，以撫諭軍民為名。

translations.literal: Tianxi avoided the distant Xianshan and first arranged with Fan Zhen; Zhen sent one Li of his command, under the pretext of reassuring soldiers and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi, finding Xianshan too distant, arranged first with Fan Zhen, who sent a certain Li from his command under the pretext of reassuring soldiers and civilians.

sentences.zh: 皋率軍士迎于東門，知朝廷圖己，陰為之備，李猶豫不敢發。

translations.literal: Gao led soldiers to welcome them at the east gate; knowing the court plotted against him, he secretly made preparations; Li hesitated and did not dare act.
