translations.idiomatic: Gao led soldiers to welcome them at the east gate. Learning that the court plotted against him, he made secret preparations. Li hesitated and did not dare strike.

sentences.zh: 皋館天錫于望崧樓，隱毒於食，天錫遂中毒而死。

translations.literal: Gao lodged Tianxi at Wangsong Tower and hid poison in his food; Tianxi thus died of poisoning.
translations.idiomatic: Gao lodged Tianxi at Wangsong Tower and hid poison in his food. Tianxi died of poisoning.

sentences.zh: 皋後為大元兵所殺。

translations.literal: Gao was later killed by the Great Yuan army.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was later killed by the armies of the Great Yuan.

sentences.zh: 楊鵬字飛卿，能詩。

translations.literal: Yang Peng, courtesy name Feiqing, could write poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Peng, courtesy name Feiqing, was a poet.

sentences.zh: 愛申，逸其族與名，或曰一名忙哥。

translations.literal: Ai Shen — his clan and given name are lost; some say his other name was Mangge.
translations.idiomatic: Ai Shen — his clan and given name are lost to history; some say he was also called Mangge.

sentences.zh: 本虢縣鎮防軍，累功遷軍中總領。

translations.literal: Originally of the Guo County garrison defense force, through repeated merit he was promoted to army commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He began in the Guo County garrison defense force and, through repeated merit, rose to commander-in-chief of the army.

sentences.zh: 李文秀據秦州，宣宗詔鳳翔軍討之，軍圍秦州城。

translations.literal: Li Wenxiu held Qinzhou; Emperor Xuanzong ordered the Fengxiang army to suppress him, and the army besieged the city of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Wenxiu seized Qinzhou, Emperor Xuanzong ordered the Fengxiang army against him, and they besieged the city.

sentences.zh: 時愛申在軍中，有罪當死。

translations.literal: At that time Ai Shen was in the army and had committed a crime for which he should die.
translations.idiomatic: Ai Shen was then in the army and had committed a capital offense.

sentences.zh: 宣宗問之樞帥，有知其名者奏此人將帥材，忠實可倚。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong asked the marshal of the privy council; one who knew his name memorialized that this man had the talent of a general and was loyal and dependable.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked the privy marshal, and one who knew him reported that the man had the talent of a general and was loyal and dependable.

sentences.zh: 宣宗命馳赦之，以為德順節度使、行元帥府事。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong ordered a hurried pardon and made him military commissioner of Defu and acting head of the marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a hurried pardon and made him military commissioner of Defu, acting head of the marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 正大四年春，大兵西來，擬以德順為坐夏之所，德順無軍，人甚危之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year of Zhengda, the great army came from the west; they intended Defu as their summer camp; Defu had no army, and people were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year of Zhengda the great army came from the west, intending to make Defu their summer camp. Defu had no army, and the situation was desperate.

sentences.zh: 愛申識鳳翔馬肩龍舜卿者可與謀事，乃遺書招之，肩龍得書欲行，鳳翔總管禾速嘉國鑒以大兵方進，吾城可恃，德順決不可守，勸勿往。

translations.literal: Ai Shen knew that Ma Jianlong Shunqing of Fengxiang could be consulted on affairs; he therefore sent a letter summoning him; Jianlong received the letter and wished to go; the Fengxiang overseer Hesujia Guojian said the great army was just advancing, our city could be relied on, Defu certainly could not be held — he urged him not to go.
translations.idiomatic: Ai Shen knew that Ma Jianlong Shunqing of Fengxiang was a man to consult. He sent a letter summoning him. Jianlong wished to go, but Fengxiang overseer Hesujia Guojian urged him not to: the great army was advancing, their own city could be held, but Defu could not be defended.

sentences.zh: 肩龍曰：「愛申平生未嘗識我，一見許為知己。

translations.literal: Jianlong said, "Ai Shen never knew me in his life, yet at one meeting he called me his intimate friend.
translations.idiomatic: Jianlong said, "Ai Shen never knew me in his life, yet at one meeting he called me his friend.

sentences.zh: 我知德順不可守，往則必死，然以知己故。

translations.literal: I know Defu cannot be held; if I go I shall surely die — yet for the sake of this intimate friend.
translations.idiomatic: I know Defu cannot be held and that if I go I shall surely die — yet for the sake of that friendship.

sentences.zh: 不得不為之死耳。

translations.literal: I cannot but die for him.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot but die for him.

sentences.zh: 」乃舉行橐付族父，明為死別，冒險而去。

translations.literal: " He then handed his traveling bag to a clansman elder, plainly taking leave as for death, and went off through peril.
translations.idiomatic: " He gave his traveling bag to a clansman elder, plainly taking leave as for death, and set out through peril.

sentences.zh: 既至，不數日受圍，城中惟有義兵鄉軍八九千人，大兵舉天下之勢攻之。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, within a few days they were besieged; in the city there were only righteous militia and local troops of eight or nine thousand; the great army brought the momentum of the whole realm to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived, the city was besieged within days. Only eight or nine thousand militia and local troops remained inside, while the great army brought the full weight of the realm against them.

sentences.zh: 愛申假舜卿鳳翔總管府判官，守禦一與共之。

translations.literal: Ai Shen borrowed Shunqing as judge of the Fengxiang overseer's headquarters; defense and garrison they shared together.
translations.idiomatic: Ai Shen borrowed Shunqing from the Fengxiang overseer's staff as judge, and they shared the defense together.

sentences.zh: 凡攻百二十晝夜，力盡乃破，愛申以劍自剄，時年五十三。

translations.literal: In all they attacked for one hundred twenty days and nights; when strength was exhausted it fell; Ai Shen ran himself through with a sword; he was then fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: The siege lasted one hundred twenty days and nights. When strength was exhausted the city fell. Ai Shen ran himself through with a sword. He was fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 軍中募生致肩龍，而不知所終。

translations.literal: In the army they offered a reward to take Jianlong alive, but his end was unknown.
translations.idiomatic: The army offered a reward to take Jianlong alive, but his fate was never known.

sentences.zh: 台諫有言當贈德順死事者官，以勸中外。

translations.literal: The censorate and remonstrance officials said that those who died for Defu should be granted offices, to encourage within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Censors and remonstrance officials urged that offices be granted to those who had died for Defu, to encourage loyalty throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 詔各贈官，配食褒忠廟。

translations.literal: An edict granted each a posthumous office and enshrined them for sacrifice in the Hall of Rewarding Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted each a posthumous office and enshrined them in the Hall of Rewarding Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 馬肩龍

translations.literal: Ma Jianlong
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jianlong

translations.literal: (Supplementary)
translations.idiomatic: (Supplementary biography)

sentences.zh: 肩龍字舜卿，宛平人。

translations.literal: Jianlong, courtesy name Shunqing, was a native of Wanping.
translations.idiomatic: Jianlong, courtesy name Shunqing, came from Wanping.

sentences.zh: 先世遼大族，有知興中府者，故人號興中馬氏。

translations.literal: His forebears were a great clan of Liao; one had governed Xingzhong Prefecture, and therefore people called them the Ma clan of Xingzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears were a great clan of Liao. One had governed Xingzhong Prefecture, and people called them the Ma clan of Xingzhong.

sentences.zh: 祖大中，金初登科，節度全、錦兩州。

translations.literal: His grandfather Dazhong passed the examinations at the beginning of Jin and served as military commissioner of Quan and Jin prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Dazhong passed the examinations at the founding of Jin and served as military commissioner of Quan and Jin.

sentences.zh: 父成誼，明昌五年登科，仕為京兆府路統軍司判官。

translations.literal: His father Chengyi passed the examinations in the fifth year of Mingchang and served as judge of the Jingzhao Circuit Commandery-in-Chief Office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chengyi passed the examinations in the fifth year of Mingchang and served as judge of the Jingzhao Circuit commandery-in-chief office.

sentences.zh: 肩龍在太學有賦聲。

translations.literal: Jianlong at the Imperial Academy had a reputation for fu composition.
translations.idiomatic: At the Imperial Academy Jianlong was known for his fu compositions.

sentences.zh: 宣宗初，有誣宗室從坦殺人，將置之死。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanzong's reign, someone falsely accused the imperial clansman Congtan of murder, and he was about to be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xuanzong's reign, the imperial clansman Congtan was falsely accused of murder and faced execution.

sentences.zh: 人不敢言其冤，肩龍上書，大略謂：「從坦有將帥材，少出其右者，臣一介書生，無用于世，願代從坦死，留為天子將兵。

translations.literal: No one dared speak of his injustice; Jianlong submitted a memorial, in substance saying, "Congtan has the talent of a general; few surpass him. Your servant is a mere scholar, of no use in the world — I wish to die in Congtan's place and remain to lead troops for the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: No one dared speak of his innocence. Jianlong submitted a memorial saying, in substance, "Congtan has the talent of a general; few surpass him. I am a mere scholar, of no use to the world — I wish to die in his place and remain to lead troops for the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」書奏，詔問：「汝與從坦交分厚歟？

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, an edict asked, "Are you and Congtan bound by deep friendship?
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial arrived, the emperor asked, "Are you and Congtan close friends?

sentences.zh: 」肩龍對曰：「臣知有從坦，從坦未嘗識臣。

translations.literal: " Jianlong replied, "Your servant knows of Congtan; Congtan has never known your servant.
translations.idiomatic: " Jianlong replied, "I know of Congtan, but Congtan has never known me.

sentences.zh: 從坦冤人，不敢言，臣以死保之。

translations.literal: Congtan is a wronged man; none dares speak; your servant guarantees him with my death.
translations.idiomatic: Congtan is innocent, yet none dares speak. I guarantee him with my life.

sentences.zh: 」宣宗感悟，赦從坦，授肩龍東平錄事，委行省試驗。

translations.literal: " Emperor Xuanzong was moved and pardoned Congtan; he appointed Jianlong recorder of Dongping and entrusted him to the Branch Secretariat for examination.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was moved, pardoned Congtan, appointed Jianlong recorder of Dongping, and referred him to the Branch Secretariat for examination.

sentences.zh: 宰相侯摯與語不契，留數月罷歸，將渡河，與排岸官紛競，搜篋中，得軍馬糧料名數及利害數事，疑其為奸人偵伺者，系歸德獄根勘。

translations.literal: The chief councilor Hou Zhi did not agree with him in conversation; after several months he was dismissed and sent home; as he was about to cross the river he quarreled with the shore patrol officer; they searched his bag and found lists of army horses, grain, and several matters of strategic advantage and harm; they suspected him a spy of traitors and imprisoned him in Guide for thorough investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Chief councilor Hou Zhi took no liking to him in conversation. After several months he was dismissed and sent home. About to cross the river, he quarreled with a shore patrol officer who searched his bag and found lists of army horses, grain supplies, and several items of strategic intelligence. Suspecting him a spy, they imprisoned him in Guide for investigation.

sentences.zh: 適從坦至，立救出之。

translations.literal: Congtan happened to arrive and at once rescued him.
translations.idiomatic: Congtan happened to arrive and rescued him at once.

sentences.zh: 正大三年，客鳳翔，元帥愛申深器重之，至是，同死於難。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengda he was a guest at Fengxiang; Marshal Ai Shen deeply valued him; at this time they died together in the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhengda he was a guest at Fengxiang, where Marshal Ai Shen held him in high regard. In the end they died together in the siege.

sentences.zh: 禹顯，雁門人。

translations.literal: Yu Xian, a native of Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xian came from Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，隸上党公張開，累以戰功授義勝軍節度使、兼沁州招撫副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou he served under Duke Shangdang Zhang Kai; through repeated battle merit he was appointed Military Commissioner of the Yisheng Army and concurrently Vice Pacification Commissioner of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenyou he served under Duke Shangdang Zhang Kai. Repeated battle honors made him military commissioner of the Yisheng Army and vice pacification commissioner of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 元光二年四月，大帥達兒泬、按察兒攻河東，張開遣顯扼龍豬穀，夾攻敗之，擒元帥韓光國，獲輜重甲仗甚眾，追至祁縣而還，所曆州縣悉複之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Yuanguang, the great generals Da'erba and Ancha'er attacked Hedong; Zhang Kai sent Xian to hold Longzhu Valley; with pincer attack they defeated them, captured the marshal Han Guangguo, took very many baggage trains, armor, and weapons, pursued to Qi County and returned, and all prefectures and counties they passed were recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year of Yuanguang the great generals Da'erba and Ancha'er attacked Hedong. Zhang Kai sent Xian to hold Longzhu Valley. A pincer attack routed them, capturing marshal Han Guangguo and vast stores of baggage, armor, and weapons. They pursued to Qi County and returned, recovering every prefecture and county along the way.

sentences.zh: 顯將軍三百人，守襄垣，八年不遷。

translations.literal: Xian commanded three hundred soldiers and held Xiangyuan, without transfer for eight years.
translations.idiomatic: Xian held Xiangyuan with three hundred men and received no transfer for eight years.

sentences.zh: 大帥嘗集河朔步騎數萬攻之，至於數四不能拔。

translations.literal: The great marshal once gathered tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry from north of the Yellow River to attack; as many as four times they could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy marshal once gathered tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry from north of the river to attack — four times without success.

sentences.zh: 既而，戰于玉女寨，大獲。

translations.literal: Soon afterward they fought at Jade Maiden Stockade and won a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward they fought at Jade Maiden Stockade and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 開言于朝，權元帥右都監。

translations.literal: Kai spoke to the court, and he was made acting Marshal's Right Overseer.
translations.idiomatic: Kai reported to court, and Xian was made acting marshal's right overseer.

sentences.zh: 正大六年冬十二月，軍內變，城破被擒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter in the sixth year of Zhengda, there was mutiny within the army; the city fell and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the sixth year of Zhengda the army mutinied. The city fell and he was captured.

sentences.zh: 帥義之，不欲加害。

translations.literal: The marshal honored his righteousness and did not wish to harm him.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy commander admired his spirit and did not wish to harm him.

sentences.zh: 初以鐵繩鈐之，既而密與舊部曲二十人遁去，聞上黨公軍複振，將往從之。

translations.literal: At first they shackled him with iron chains; before long he secretly fled with twenty old retainers; hearing that Duke Shangdang's army had revived, he was about to go join them.
translations.idiomatic: At first they shackled him with iron chains. Before long he fled secretly with twenty old retainers, intending to join Duke Shangdang's revived army.

sentences.zh: 大兵四向來追，顯適與負釜一兵相失，乞飯山寺中，僧走報焉，被執不屈死，時年四十一。

translations.literal: The great army pursued from four directions; Xian happened to lose contact with one soldier carrying a cauldron; he begged food at a mountain temple; a monk ran to report; he was seized, would not yield, and died; he was then forty-one.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy pursued from four directions. Xian lost contact with a soldier carrying a cooking pot and begged food at a mountain temple. A monk ran to report him. Seized, he would not yield and was killed. He was forty-one.

sentences.zh: 張邦憲

translations.literal: Zhang Bangxian
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bangxian

sentences.zh: 秦州人張邦憲，字正叔，登正大中進士第，為永固令。

translations.literal: Zhang Bangxian of Qinzhou, courtesy name Zhengshu, passed the jinshi examination in the middle Zhengda period and served as magistrate of Yonggu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bangxian of Qinzhou, courtesy name Zhengshu, passed the jinshi examination in the middle Zhengda period and served as magistrate of Yonggu.

sentences.zh: 天興二年，避兵徐州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianxing he fled the armies to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianxing he fled the war to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 卓翼率兵至城，邦憲被執，將驅之北，邦憲罵曰：「我進士也，誤蒙朝廷用為邑長，可從汝曹反耶！

translations.literal: Zhuo Yi led troops to the city; Bangxian was seized and about to be driven north; Bangxian cursed, saying, "I am a jinshi graduate; I was wrongly used by the court as a district chief — how could I follow you rebels!
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo Yi led troops to the city. Seized and about to be driven north, Bangxian cursed them: "I am a jinshi graduate whom the court wrongly made a district chief — how could I follow you rebels!

sentences.zh: 」遂遇害。

translations.literal: " He was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then killed.

sentences.zh: 劉全者，彭城民也。

translations.literal: Liu Quan was a commoner of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Quan was a commoner of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 率鄉鄰數百避兵沫溝，推為砦主。

translations.literal: He led several hundred fellow townsmen to flee the armies to Mogou and was made stockade chief.
translations.idiomatic: He led several hundred neighbors to flee the war to Mogou Ravine, where they made him stockade chief.

sentences.zh: 北兵至徐，盡俘其老幼，全父亦在其中，北兵質之以招全，全縛其人送徐州，因竊其父以歸。

translations.literal: When northern troops reached Xu, they captured all their old and young; Quan's father was among them; the northern army held him hostage to summon Quan; Quan bound their men and sent them to Xuzhou, then secretly brought his father back.
translations.idiomatic: When northern troops reached Xu they captured all the old and young, including Quan's father, whom they held hostage to lure Quan. Quan bound their men and sent them to Xuzhou, then secretly brought his father home.

sentences.zh: 徐帥益都嘉其忠，承制以為昭信校尉，遙領彭城縣尉。

translations.literal: The Xu commander Yidu praised his loyalty and, by provisional order, made him Colonel of Manifest Trust, holding in absentia the post of Pengcheng county lieutenant.
translations.idiomatic: The Xu commander Yidu praised his loyalty and, by provisional order, made him Colonel of Manifest Trust with the absentee post of Pengcheng county lieutenant.

sentences.zh: 後遇國用安，怒其不附己，見殺。

translations.literal: Later he encountered Guo Yong'an, who was angry that he would not attach himself to him, and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Later he encountered Guo Yong'an, who resented his refusal to submit and had him killed.
